newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurer sacks complete management board.
newsitem.headline: German insurer sacks complete management board.

text.p: German insurance mutual society Koelner Postversicherung VVaG (KPV) has replaced its complete management board following massive losses from property deals.
The company said that, following the departure in December 1996 of board member Dieter Hajek, the two other board members would leave KPV.
The new management consists of chief executive officer Alfred Waiss and board members Guenter Geissler, Werner Schorn and Bernd Walz.

The new board is identical with the management of fellow mutual Vereinigte Postversicherung VVaG (VPV), Stuttgart, with which KPV is to merge next year. Both KPV and VPV were originally post office staff mutuals.
Former chief executive Hartwig Drueck has signed a termination agreement and will leave KPV at the end of July.

Board member Hans Wilhelm Porschen was dismissed from his post. He is likely to take legal steps against the company's move. "But we are in this case also seeking a termination agreement," new board member Bernd Walz said.

The decision to sever ties with Drueck and Porschen had been taken by the supervisory board because the whole management board had to take responsibility for the company's business affairs, Walz said.

KPV, which had premium income of 425 million marks ($242 million) in 1996, needed to make write-downs of around 48 million marks on real estate, Walz said. In addition, there would be sizeable write-downs of mortgage loans, said Walz.
Dieter Hajek, who left in December, was directly in charge of the insurer's property investments.
Germany's insurance supervisory authority Bundesaufsichtsamt fuer das Versicherungswesen (BAV) carried out checks at KPV in June, Walz confirmed.
-- Herbert Fromme, Reuters Insurance News, +49 221 512007 ($ = 1.759 German Marks)
